title: Present paginated retained Plant history

gates.name: plant_history_list_browser
gates.command: cd frontend && npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/plant-history-list.spec.ts

verify: Independent active/archived browser verification covers complete history continuation, source filtering, safe refs, cursor/authorization failures, and no Timeline replay/write or local-path behavior.
evidence_required: FT-016-AC-022 RED: no PWA paginated Plant-history consumer exists; GREEN: active and archived-authorized pages render complete stable history and safe audit/export refs while invalid cursor/filter and denied access fail with no write/replay edge; decisive comparison: response/DOM/cursor transcript plus Timeline/path/request inspection; artifact: retained-history evidence under .tasks/TASK-102-T3-FT-016-W3/.
purpose: Expose complete paginated retained Plant history independently of the current Plant card.
success_outcome: Authorized users can traverse exact active or archived-retained history and safe refs with canonical continuation/errors while the PWA has no Timeline replay/write or storage access.
anti_goals: Do not implement the Plant card, read/replay timeline.jsonl, query PostgreSQL directly, or build export packages.
Do not make archived retained-history operational or materialize new rows/work.

forbidden_scope: Timeline replay/write or direct file access
stop_conditions: Required history data is absent from Plant History HTTP and would require a direct data bypass.
Retained presentation would create or advance operational state.

constraints: Primary owner is Operator PWA; Plant History owns projection, retained authorization, and cursor behavior.
Use backend-selected active/retained mode and opaque cursor values.
invariants: Timeline remains append-only audit/export and never becomes PWA runtime authority.
Archived history presentation creates no write or operational transition.
verification_targets: FT-016-AC-022: stable complete history pagination, source filters, retained authorization, safe refs, cursor failures, and zero write/replay edge.
T3 harm proof uses isolated history rows and verifies denied/malformed reads leave no mutation or local-path/auth residue.
